roles.description: How the consumption arrives: 'request', 'parameter', or 'response.<status>'. A nested edge carries the roles of the direct class it hangs off, so a client can filter 'everything this response drags in' without re-walking the graph.

via.title: Via
via.description: For a nested edge, the shortest chain of classes from the directly consumed one to this class's parent. Empty for a direct edge.

depth.title: Depth
depth.description: Hops from the directly consumed class — 0 for direct, len(via) otherwise.

ConsumptionEdgeOut.title: ConsumptionEdgeOut
ConsumptionEdgeOut.description:
One operation consuming one class — an edge of the combined lens (DUW-1.4).

``direct`` is the solid amber edge the legend calls "direct schema in request/response";
``nested`` is the dashed rose "nested via parent class", and its ``via`` chain names the
parents it hangs off. An operation that both names a class and reaches it through another is
one *direct* edge, not two: the canvas draws one line between two nodes.

version_id.title: Version Id
version_id.description: Project version identifier or semantic version label, depending on context.

domain_id.title: Domain Id
domain_id.description: The folder scoped to, when scope is 'domain'. Null means the 'shared/' bucket, not 'unscoped' — read scope to tell them apart.

path_ids.title: Path Ids
path_ids.description: The paths scoped to, when scope is 'path_ids'.

class_ids.title: Class Ids
class_ids.description: The class filter applied, if any. Combines with either path scope: it narrows the class side of every edge, never the path side.

missing_ids.title: Missing Ids
missing_ids.description: Ids the caller named — paths or classes — that this version does not hold. Reported rather than dropped: a silently short answer would leave a hole on the canvas with no way to know why.

edges.title: Edges
edges.description: One entry per operation↔class pair, ordered by pathname, then method, then direct before nested, then class name.

paths.title: Paths
paths.description: The same facts rolled up per path — the tree's per-path Schemas block. Paths that consume nothing are absent rather than present-and-empty.

link_count.title: Link Count
link_count.description: Edges returned — what the canvas draws and the status bar's 'N schema↔path links' chip counts.

path_link_count.title: Path Link Count
path_link_count.description: Distinct path↔class pairs, for a status bar that counts links per path rather than per operation.

depth_cap.title: Depth Cap
depth_cap.description: How far a nested edge may sit from its direct root.

depth_capped.title: Depth Capped
depth_capped.description: A reference graph continued past depth_cap, so some far nested edges are not in this answer.

edge_limit.title: Edge Limit
edge_limit.description: Most edges one response may carry.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: The edge list was cut at edge_limit. Narrow the scope — by domain, by path set, or by class set — rather than paging: an edge only means something beside the members it connects.

ConsumptionIndex.title: ConsumptionIndex
ConsumptionIndex.description:
Which operations consume which classes, and how (DUW-1.4).

Computed on read from the version's own content, never persisted, and content-addressed with a
strong ``ETag`` so a repeat read is a 304 until the version changes.

ConsumptionPath.title: ConsumptionPath
ConsumptionPath.description: One path's ``Schemas`` block — its classes rolled up across its operations (DUW-1.4).

class_id.title: Class Id
class_id.description: Class identifier the resource is attached to.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: 'direct' or 'nested', direct winning when a path's operations disagree.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: Every role across the path's operations.

badge.title: Badge
badge.description: What the tree prints beside the row: a status code ('200'), 'body', 'param', or 'nested'.

ConsumptionPathClass.title: ConsumptionPathClass
ConsumptionPathClass.description: One schema row of a path's ``Schemas`` block in the tree (DUW-1.4).

class_id.title: Class Id
class_id.description: Class identifier the resource is attached to.

ConsumptionVia.title: ConsumptionVia
ConsumptionVia.description: One hop on the parent chain that reaches a nested class (DUW-1.4).

case_id.title: Case Id
case_id.description: Stable identifier, derived from the operation, the source, and what distinguishes this case from its siblings. The same version and options always yield the same id.

source.title: Source
source.description: One of the case sources — where this case came from.

source_detail.title: Source Detail
source_detail.description: What distinguishes this case within its source — an example name, a mutation kind, or the parameter a negative case targets.

source_pointer.title: Source Pointer
source_pointer.description: JSON Pointer to the case's origin: into the source document for a declared example, into the body for a generated violation.

title.title: Title
title.description: Short human-readable name, unique within the operation.

description.title: Description
description.example: A pet available for adoption in the store.

synthetic.title: Synthetic
synthetic.description: False only when the request body is an example the author wrote. True for every generated payload, so the label travels with the case.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: The operation's tags, for filtered runs.

ContractCase.title: ContractCase
ContractCase.description: One executable case: a request, its provenance, and its expected outcome.

status_codes.title: Status Codes
status_codes.description: Acceptable status codes, from the contract's own declarations. A wildcard (`2XX`, `4XX`) means the range is acceptable.

status_declared.title: Status Declared
status_declared.description: Whether `status_codes` came from the document. `false` means the compiler fell back to a range because the contract declared none — a weaker assertion, and one the suite states rather than hides.

response_schema_id.title: Response Schema Id
response_schema_id.description: Key into the manifest's `schemas` map for the schema the response body must satisfy. Null when the contract declares no response schema.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: One sentence explaining why this outcome is expected.

ContractCaseExpectation.title: ContractCaseExpectation
ContractCaseExpectation.description: What a conforming implementation must do with the case's request.

path.title: Path
path.description: The template with every path parameter substituted and percent-encoded — append it to the target's base URL to get the request URL.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.description: Parameter values, sorted by location then name.

has_body.title: Has Body
has_body.description: Whether the case sends a body at all. Distinguishes 'no body' from 'a body whose value is null', which are different requests.

body.title: Body
body.description: The request body, when there is one.

media_type.title: Media Type
media_type.description: Media type the body is sent as.

ContractCaseRequest.title: ContractCaseRequest
ContractCaseRequest.description: The request a case sends, complete enough to execute against a chosen target.

value.title: Value
value.description: Wire value, already serialized as a string.

origin.title: Origin
origin.description: Where the value came from: `declared_example`, `default`, `enum`, or `generated`.

ContractRequestParameter.title: ContractRequestParameter
ContractRequestParameter.description: One parameter value a case sends, with the evidence behind it.

options.description: Compiler options; hashed into the suite digest recorded on the run.

idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key
idempotency_key.description: Evidence upload retry key; forwarded to the verification-runs store.

context.title: Context
context.description: Non-secret CI context (commit, branch, workflow URL).

ContractRunRequest.title: ContractRunRequest
ContractRunRequest.description:
What to execute against which target.

Compiler options are optional and default to the same defaults as suite compilation, so a
digest recorded in evidence matches ``POST …/suite`` with the same options.

ok.title: Ok
ok.description: Whether the suite executed and evidence was recorded.

version_ref.title: Version Ref
version_ref.description: The version reference exactly as requested.

suite_digest.title: Suite Digest
suite_digest.description: Digest of the suite that was executed, when compiled.

run.description: Immutable evidence record when `ok` is true.

created.title: Created
created.description: True when evidence was newly written; False on idempotent replay.

error.description: Populated when `ok` is false: stable taxonomy code plus remediation.

ContractRunResponse.title: ContractRunResponse
ContractRunResponse.description: The outcome of one contract run attempt.

options.description: Compiler options. They are echoed on the manifest and hashed into its digest, so the same version compiled with the same options always yields the same suite.

ContractSuiteCompileRequest.title: ContractSuiteCompileRequest
ContractSuiteCompileRequest.description:
What to compile for the version named in the URL.

The options are wrapped rather than inlined so the request can grow a sibling field without
changing the meaning of an existing body. An empty body compiles everything under the
default options.

digest.title: Digest
digest.description: `sha256:<hex>` over the canonical bytes of this manifest with `digest` itself removed. Two suites with the same digest are the same suite.

options.description: The options this suite was compiled with, normalized.

source.description: Where the compiled version came from.

cases.title: Cases
cases.description: Every case, grouped by operation (sorted by key) then by source order.

schemas.title: Schemas
schemas.description: Response schemas referenced by `expect.response_schema_id`, keyed so identical types are carried once.

findings.title: Findings
findings.description: What was not compiled, and what was compiled weakly — sorted by code, operation, then message. Never empty merely because the suite is large.

counts.title: Counts
counts.description: Case counts by source, plus `cases`, `operations_compiled`, `operations_skipped`, and `findings`.

ContractSuiteManifest.title: ContractSuiteManifest
ContractSuiteManifest.description: The compiled suite: everything a runner needs, and everything a reviewer should know.

seed.title: Seed
seed.description: Seed for generated values. The same version and seed always produce the same payloads; change it to sample different values of the same shapes.

include_declared_examples.title: Include Declared Examples
include_declared_examples.description: Compile the examples declared in the source document into request cases.

include_generated.title: Include Generated
include_generated.description: Compile schema-valid generated bodies (minimal, full, and branches).

include_branches.title: Include Branches
include_branches.description: Include one generated body per polymorphic (`oneOf`/`anyOf`/`if`) alternative of a request body. Ignored when generated cases are off.

include_negative.title: Include Negative
include_negative.description: Compile the negative cases: a missing required body, a missing required query parameter, a wrong-typed parameter, and single-constraint body violations.

verify_examples.title: Verify Examples
verify_examples.description: Check every declared example against the schema governing it, and compile only the conforming ones. A non-conforming example is reported, never compiled: it would fail a correct implementation.

include_response_schemas.title: Include Response Schemas
include_response_schemas.description: Carry the response schema each success case must satisfy in the manifest, so a runner validates responses without resolving the version again.

max_example_cases_per_operation.title: Max Example Cases Per Operation
max_example_cases_per_operation.description: Cap on declared-example cases per operation.

max_generated_cases_per_operation.title: Max Generated Cases Per Operation
max_generated_cases_per_operation.description: Cap on generated valid bodies per operation. The minimal and full bodies come first; the remainder of the budget goes to polymorphic branches.

max_negative_cases_per_operation.title: Max Negative Cases Per Operation
max_negative_cases_per_operation.description: Cap on negative cases per operation. Structural negatives (missing body, missing parameter, wrong-typed parameter) are compiled first; the remainder of the budget goes to single-constraint body violations.

max_operations.title: Max Operations
max_operations.description: Cap on compiled operations. Truncation is always reported as a finding.

operations.title: Operations
operations.description: Restrict compilation to these operation keys (`GET /pets/{petId}`). Omit for every operation. A key that matches nothing is reported as a finding.

ContractSuiteOptions.title: ContractSuiteOptions
ContractSuiteOptions.description:
What to compile, and how much of it.

Every field is part of the suite's identity: the options are echoed in the manifest and
hashed into its digest, so "the same version compiled the same way" is a checkable claim
rather than a hope. Defaults compile the whole suite.

ok.title: Ok
ok.description: Whether a suite could be compiled at all.

version_ref.title: Version Ref
version_ref.description: The reference exactly as it was requested.

manifest.description: The compiled suite. Present whenever `ok` is true — including when it contains no cases, which is a real answer about a version that declares no operations.

error.description: Populated when `ok` is false: stable taxonomy code plus remediation.

ContractSuiteResponse.title: ContractSuiteResponse
ContractSuiteResponse.description: The compiled suite for one version.

title.title: Title
title.description: Fallback API title when the source has none.

version.title: Version
version.description: Fallback API version when the source declares none.

servers.title: Servers
servers.description: Fallback server URLs when the source declares no servers.

ConversionDefaultsRequest.title: ConversionDefaultsRequest
ConversionDefaultsRequest.description:
User-supplied defaults that close cheap gaps *before* a catalog → OpenAPI conversion commits
(MFI-22.6).

All optional; each is applied to the emitted document only where the source model left the
corresponding construct empty (a default never overwrites a value the source declared). Mirrors
the inline defaults the preview screen (MFI-22.4) collects and the ``ConversionDefaults`` the job
(MFI-22.5) consumes.

itemId.title: Itemid
itemId.description: Catalog item id, on the catalog surface.

projectId.title: Projectid
projectId.description: Target Project id, on the project surface.

sourceHash.title: Sourcehash
sourceHash.description: Digest of the source text converted, or null.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: The bounded manifest summary of the stored snapshot; null when unavailable.

page.title: Page
page.description: One page of the stored graph's edges + nodes; null when unavailable.

ConversionEvidenceResponse.title: ConversionEvidenceResponse
ConversionEvidenceResponse.description:
One page of a historical conversion's stored evidence graph (CPDO-3.3).

Serves the exact approved manifest from the content-addressed snapshot store — never a rebuild —
so the evidence shown is the evidence the conversion was committed with, regardless of how the
source or the converter changed since. ``summary``/``page`` are ``null`` exactly when
``snapshot.status`` is ``unavailable``; degrade is HTTP 200, never a 5xx.

createdBy.title: Createdby
createdBy.description: User id that ran the conversion.

reconverted.title: Reconverted
reconverted.description: True when this conversion superseded a prior conversion of the source.

conversionMode.title: Conversionmode
conversionMode.description: passthrough / typespec_native / lossy, from the converter tool versions.

sourceProjectId.title: Sourceprojectid
sourceProjectId.description: Catalog item id the conversion ran from; None when the item was hard-deleted.

sourceProjectName.title: Sourceprojectname
sourceProjectName.description: Display name of the source catalog item.

sourceVersionId.title: Sourceversionid
sourceVersionId.description: Source revision row id (versions.id) that was converted.

targetProjectDeleted.title: Targetprojectdeleted
targetProjectDeleted.description: True when the target Project has since been (soft-)deleted.

targetVersionLabel.title: Targetversionlabel
targetVersionLabel.description: Semantic version label of the produced revision (e.g. '1.0.1').

targetVersionRecordId.title: Targetversionrecordid
targetVersionRecordId.description: Row id (versions.id) of the produced revision — the target revision this snapshot is linked to.

toolVersions.title: Toolversions
toolVersions.description: Converter tool versions that produced the conversion.

defaults.title: Defaults
defaults.description: Normalized gap-filling defaults the conversion was committed with, from the stored manifest summary.

schemaVersion.title: Schemaversion
schemaVersion.description: Manifest contract version the stored summary was built under.

manifestHash.title: Manifesthash
manifestHash.description: Content-addressed evidence snapshot id; None on rows recorded before manifests existed (CPDO-1.3).

sourceHash.title: Sourcehash
sourceHash.description: sha256:-prefixed digest of the exact source text converted; None on rows recorded before CPDO-3.3. Differing from currentSourceHash marks the evidence historic.

snapshotAvailable.title: Snapshotavailable
snapshotAvailable.description: True when the full evidence snapshot is stored and its graph can be replayed.

ConversionProvenanceEntry.title: ConversionProvenanceEntry
ConversionProvenanceEntry.description:
One row of a conversion's provenance history (CPDO-3.3, #4803).

Projected from the append-only ``apiome.conversion_provenance`` ledger with the V215 history
enrichment: whether the content-addressed evidence snapshot for this conversion actually exists
(``snapshotAvailable``), and the display coordinates of both the source catalog item and the
target Project. Empty-string ledger sentinels (``projection_manifest_hash``, ``source_hash``)
serialize as ``null`` — "recorded before snapshots existed" — rather than leaking storage
defaults into the wire contract.

status.title: Status
status.description: Whether the stored evidence graph is being served.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the snapshot is unavailable; null when available.

ConversionSnapshotState.title: ConversionSnapshotState
ConversionSnapshotState.description:
Whether a historical conversion's evidence snapshot could be served, and why not (CPDO-3.3).

A missing snapshot is a truthful, expected state — never an error: ``predates_snapshots`` for
rows committed before manifests were persisted, ``snapshot_missing`` when the row names a hash
with no stored snapshot (a best-effort write that failed), ``unreadable`` when the stored
manifest no longer validates against this reader's contract version.

ConversionSupport.title: ConversionSupport
ConversionSupport.description: Whether this format participates in the canonical conversion graph.

support.description: Whether a conversion path exists at all.

canonical_formats.title: Canonical Formats
canonical_formats.description: Declared format keys that resolve to a registered normalizer — the routes onto the canonical model, sorted. Empty when the adapter normalizes in-adapter.

normalizes_in_adapter.title: Normalizes In Adapter
normalizes_in_adapter.description: True when no registered normalizer claims any declared key and the adapter builds the canonical model itself. Not a gap — a different route.

declared_formats.title: Declared Formats
declared_formats.description: Every format key the adapter declares, sorted. A mix of normalizer keys and detection aliases, so a key here without a normalizer is not by itself a missing route.

note.title: Note
note.description: One line on the conversion route or its absence.

ConversionSupportEntry.title: ConversionSupportEntry
ConversionSupportEntry.description:
Whether this format participates in the conversion graph, and by which route.

The route matters less than the *fact*: an adapter that persists a catalog item has, by
contract, produced a canonical model for it, so it can reach every export destination. What
varies is how — through a normalizer registered under one of the adapter's declared format
keys, or inside the adapter itself — and whether it can run here at all.

target.title: Target
target.description: Conversion target format (only 'openapi' today).

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: When true, return the fidelity report with no side effects; when false, commit.

anyOf.description: Request body for convert catalog item.

defaults.description: Optional user-supplied fallbacks applied only where the source is empty.

ConvertCatalogItemRequest.title: ConvertCatalogItemRequest
ConvertCatalogItemRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /v1/catalog/{tenant_slug}/{item_id}/convert`` (MFI-22.6).

Carries the conversion target (``openapi`` is the only one today, but the verb is target-generic
for future emitters), the ``dryRun`` flag (the query param is authoritative for the side-effect
decision; this mirrors it so a body-only caller still works), and the optional user defaults.

class_id.title: Class Id
class_id.description: Class identifier the resource is attached to.

CopyClassToInlineSchemaRequest.title: CopyClassToInlineSchemaRequest
CopyClassToInlineSchemaRequest.description: Request model for copying class properties to inline schema.

CoverageClass.title: CoverageClass
CoverageClass.description:
Coverage classification of one source construct in the import (IXH-3.1).

The values are the ticket's exact vocabulary. Each class is a documented view over
the shared :class:`~app.projection_taxonomy.ProjectionStatus` /
:class:`~app.projection_taxonomy.ProjectionReason` pair (see
:data:`STATUS_FOR_COVERAGE`) — never a parallel status vocabulary.

source_construct.title: Source Construct
source_construct.description: The source construct this row classifies (an entity key, a document-level attribute, or a construct class). Named ``source_construct`` (not ``construct``) so it cannot shadow pydantic's legacy ``BaseModel.construct``.

status.description: The shared CPDO-1.3 projection status this class encodes.

reason.description: The shared reason code for a non-mapped class; null for ``mapped``.

entity_key.title: Entity Key
entity_key.description: The canonical entity this row concerns, when entity-scoped.

document_scoped.title: Document Scoped
document_scoped.description: True when the row states a fact about this document; false for an adapter-level declaration (a parser limit not evaluated against this document).

capability_reference.description: The CLX-2.4 registry entry documenting the coverage gap; present on every ``not-parsed-by-adapter`` row.

CoverageEntry.title: CoverageEntry
CoverageEntry.description:
One row of the coverage ledger (IXH-3.1).

Classifies one source construct. Entity-scoped rows reference their canonical
entity by key; document-scoped rows (root-level constructs) have no entity. A
declared parser limit is marked ``document_scoped = false`` — it states an adapter
fact, not a verified fact about this document.

siteId.title: Siteid
siteId.description: Site the connection builds previews for.

previewHost.title: Previewhost
previewHost.description: Base host the immutable and alias preview URLs are derived from.

webhookSecret.title: Webhooksecret
webhookSecret.description: Webhook signing secret. Write-only: sealed at rest and never returned.

token.title: Token
token.description: Repository token. Write-only: envelope-sealed at rest and never returned.

CreateConnectionRequest.title: CreateConnectionRequest
CreateConnectionRequest.description: Register (or update) a git provider connection for a site.

subjectRef.title: Subjectref
subjectRef.description: Group catalog id or rule id.

matcherValue.title: Matchervalue
matcherValue.description: The route pattern the exception covers.

expiresAt.title: Expiresat
expiresAt.description: When it lapses. An exception that cannot lapse is policy.

releaseRef.title: Releaseref
releaseRef.description: Short human-quotable id, unique per site.

source.description: Provenance source for the record (for example human or imported).

signature.title: Signature
signature.description: Detached signature over the three digests.

status.title: Status
status.description: Initial state of the built release.

CreateReleaseRequest.title: CreateReleaseRequest
CreateReleaseRequest.description: Record a built release and its artifact.

ruleId.title: Ruleid
ruleId.description: The rule's id (the key under `rules`); findings carry it in their `rule` field.

description.title: Description
description.description: Human description; used as the base finding message.
description.example: A pet available for adoption in the store.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: Severity findings carry: error | warning | info.

given.title: Given
given.description: JSONPath expressions selecting the values the rule tests.

then.title: Then
then.description: Clauses applied to every given match.

CustomRuleOut.title: CustomRuleOut
CustomRuleOut.description: One validated custom rule from a style-guide document (GOV-1.3, #4429).

anyOf.description: Response payload for custom rule then.
Response payload for custom rule then.

field.title: Field
field.description: Property name the function tests ('@key' tests each object key); null tests the match itself.

function.title: Function
function.description: Core function: pattern, casing, enumeration, truthy, defined, undefined, length.

functionOptions.title: Functionoptions
functionOptions.description: The validated functionOptions for the function (empty when it takes none).

CustomRuleThenOut.title: CustomRuleThenOut
CustomRuleThenOut.description: One validated `then` clause of a custom rule (GOV-1.3, #4429).

yaml.title: Yaml
yaml.description: The style-guide YAML document (`rules.<id>: {description, severity, given, then}`).

CustomRulesValidateRequest.title: CustomRulesValidateRequest
CustomRulesValidateRequest.description: Request body for custom-rule DSL validation (GOV-1.3, #4429): the guide YAML source.

valid.title: Valid
valid.description: Always true on a 200 (malformed guides return HTTP 422).

rules.title: Rules
rules.description: Every validated rule, in author order.

CustomRulesValidateResponse.title: CustomRulesValidateResponse
CustomRulesValidateResponse.description: Successful validation of a custom-rule guide (GOV-1.3, #4429): the parsed rules.

status.title: Status
status.description: unavailable: nothing is able to report a status.

sentence.title: Sentence
sentence.default: DDoS protection status is unavailable because no delivery tier is attached. This is not a report that protection is off; it is the absence of anything able to report.

DdosBody.title: DdosBody
DdosBody.description:
DDoS protection status, which is *unavailable* rather than a protection state.

§29.4 promises always-on DDoS status. With no delivery tier there is nothing able to report
one, and a green "protected" badge would be a false statement rather than an inert setting —
so the only value this model can carry is the absence of a report.

DeleteExceptionResponse.title: DeleteExceptionResponse
DeleteExceptionResponse.description: The outcome of closing a carve-out early.

DeleteFunctionResponse.title: DeleteFunctionResponse
DeleteFunctionResponse.description: The outcome of a function deletion.

DeleteGrantResponse.title: DeleteGrantResponse
DeleteGrantResponse.description:
The outcome of revoking a grant, an allowance or a reference.

Revoking is a DELETE, because the absence of a row is the denial. There is no field here
reporting a ``granted`` flag, because there is no such column to report.

DeleteInsightResourceResponse.title: DeleteInsightResourceResponse
DeleteInsightResourceResponse.description: The outcome of removing an export destination, a budget or a synthetic check.

DeleteVariantResponse.title: DeleteVariantResponse
DeleteVariantResponse.description: The outcome of removing a variant.

predicate_type.title: Predicate Type
predicate_type.description: The in-toto predicate type of the wrapped statement.

signed.title: Signed
signed.description: Whether the envelope carries a signature. False when no attestation signing secret is configured on this server — the document is still well-formed, just not verifiable.

key_id.title: Key Id
key_id.description: The key id a verifier uses to select the shared secret.

envelope.title: Envelope
envelope.description: The DSSE envelope: ``payloadType`` / base64 ``payload`` / ``signatures``. Verifiable offline with the shared secret and the standard library alone.

DeliveryAttestation.title: DeliveryAttestation
DeliveryAttestation.description: The signed evidence attached to a delivered artifact.

dispatched.title: Dispatched
dispatched.description: False: no delivery tier is attached.

DeliveryDecision.title: DeliveryDecision
DeliveryDecision.description:
The gate's single verdict for one delivery.

``allow`` — nothing to say; the artifact is delivered as before.
``allow_with_warning`` — delivered, but with at least one reason the consumer should read
(validation could not run, the source carries open errors, an advisory floor was missed, or
a waiver is carrying the delivery).
``block`` — refused: no artifact bytes are produced or served.

DeliveryDimension.title: DeliveryDimension
DeliveryDimension.description: Which of the four inputs a reason came from.

blocks_delivery.title: Blocks Delivery
blocks_delivery.description: True only for ``block``. The one flag a delivery path branches on.

headline.title: Headline
headline.description: Short banner heading for the gate.

message.title: Message
message.description: The full, ready-to-display sentence. Render verbatim.

reasons.title: Reasons
reasons.description: Every named contribution, blocking reasons first. Empty on a clean allow.

target.title: Target
target.description: The resolved target format key the decision applies to.

validation_verdict.description: The emitted-artifact validation band the decision folded in, when one ran.

source_score.title: Source Score
source_score.description: The source revision's lint score, when it was graded.

source_grade.title: Source Grade
source_grade.description: The source revision's lint grade, when it was graded.

source_report_fingerprint.title: Source Report Fingerprint
source_report_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the source lint report the decision used — the same value the attestation records, so a verdict can be tied to an exact lint run.

preserved_percent.title: Preserved Percent
preserved_percent.description: The projected preserved-construct percentage the fidelity floor was measured against; null when the caller measured none.

policy.description: The tenant's export quality-policy verdict, in the one shape every import/export policy surface returns.

override.description: The override path, or its absence.

attestation.description: The signed delivery attestation. Attached once the artifact bytes exist (:func:`build_delivery_attestation`); always null on a blocked delivery, which has no artifact to attest to.

DeliveryGateReport.title: DeliveryGateReport
DeliveryGateReport.description: The delivery gate's decision for one export, with everything that produced it.

available.title: Available
available.description: Whether an override exists at all. False when nothing is blocked, when the policy forbids overrides, or when the block came from the validator (an artifact that is illegal in its target format cannot be waived).

endpoint.title: Endpoint
endpoint.description: Relative URL a waiver is recorded at (``POST``), when one may be recorded.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: The gate scope a waiver must be recorded under.

subject_key.title: Subject Key
subject_key.description: The subject key the waiver must carry — the source revision id, matching what the export pre-flight reported.

format_key.title: Format Key
format_key.description: The export target the waiver must name; a waiver for one target never covers another.

roles.title: Roles

DeliveryOverride.title: DeliveryOverride

DiffChangeKind.description: The kind of change a :class:`CanonicalDiffEntry` records.

DirectionFilter.title: DirectionFilter
DirectionFilter.description:
The ``direction`` query filter: *which capability must a row have?*

Deliberately a different vocabulary from :class:`FormatDirection`, which states what a format

write — so the filter reads as a capability question rather than an exact-match on the row's

DnsRecordBody.description: One row of the DNS table the tenant copies into their provider.

DocumentationEvidence.title: DocumentationEvidence
DocumentationEvidence.description:
Reviewed destination-format documentation metadata for a target (EFP-1.2).

A validated pointer to the authoritative specification for a destination format,
with an explicit ``documentation_unavailable`` fallback so a target with no known —
or no *applicable* — link says so truthfully rather than inventing one. When
:attr:`url` is present it is validated against the host allowlist at construction
time (:func:`validate_documentation_url`), so an unsafe link can never enter a model
instance. This supersedes EFP-1.1's per-target seed; it is now sourced per
destination (and, on a projection edge, per reason code) from this registry.

DomainAssignmentRequest.title: DomainAssignmentRequest
DomainAssignmentRequest.description:
Request model for moving a class or path between domains.

``domain_id`` is a domain UUID, the literal ``"shared"``, or null — the last two both meaning
the derived bucket. It is required rather than optional so that omitting it is a validation
error instead of a silent move to ``shared/``.

challengeRecord.title: Challengerecord
challengeRecord.description: Fully-qualified name of the TXT challenge, when one applies.

dnsTarget.title: Dnstarget
dnsTarget.description: The platform hostname this domain is pointed at.

records.title: Records
records.description: The DNS rows the tenant must publish.

DomainBody.title: DomainBody
DomainBody.description: One custom domain with everything the screen renders for it.

DomainCreateRequest.title: DomainCreateRequest
DomainCreateRequest.description:
Request model for creating a domain folder.

``slug`` is derived from ``name`` when omitted, so the common case is a single field.
``sort_order`` defaults to the end of the tree.

dnsTarget.title: Dnstarget
dnsTarget.description: The platform hostname custom domains are pointed at.

DomainListResponse.title: DomainListResponse
DomainListResponse.description: A lane's domains and the edge policy that applies to all of them.

version_id.description: Project version identifier or semantic version label, depending on context.

DomainMemberSchema.title: DomainMemberSchema
DomainMemberSchema.description:
A class or path with its current domain membership.

``name`` carries the class name or the pathname, whichever the member is, so one shape answers
both move endpoints.

DomainResponse.title: DomainResponse
DomainResponse.description: One domain, plus the edge policy, so a single-domain screen needs one call.

version_id.description: Project version identifier or semantic version label, depending on context.

DomainSchema.title: DomainSchema
DomainSchema.description:
A domain folder grouping a version's classes and paths (DUW-1.1).

``id`` is None for exactly one entry per version: the derived ``shared/`` bucket, which
collects members with no domain. A client must read ``virtual`` rather than inferring
editability from the name, since a real domain may legitimately be called anything else.

DomainUpdateRequest.title: DomainUpdateRequest
DomainUpdateRequest.description:
Request model for renaming or reordering a domain.

Every field is optional and only the supplied ones are written; renaming a domain never moves
it in the tree unless ``sort_order`` is given too.

reason.title: Reason

DroppedPointBody.description: One point that could not be correlated, and why it was not emitted.

EgressRuleBody.description: One egress allowlist entry. The row is the allowance; there is no wildcard kind.

EgressRuleResponse.description: The outcome of an egress allowlist write.

applicable.description: Whether a lint pack is registered for this target's format.

pack.description: The lint pack that ran (e.g. ``spectral:oas``), when applicable.

score.description: The 0–100 quality score, when the pack computes one.

grade.title: Grade
grade.description: The A–F letter grade, when the pack computes one.

findings.title: Findings
findings.description: The itemized lint findings (severity, rule, message, location).

EmittedArtifactLint.title: EmittedArtifactLint
EmittedArtifactLint.description:
The emitted-artifact lint report slot for one verify (MFX-5.2 → MFX-42.3).

The lint pass over the emitted artifact is **MFX-5.2**, which is not yet implemented; until it
lands, :func:`verify_export` returns ``lint: null`` and the Verify workbench renders the lint
lens's "no lint pack ran" empty state. This model documents the shape MFX-5.2 will populate so
the response contract is stable for the UI (`EmittedArtifactLintReport`).

verdict.description: The validation band: valid / invalid / skipped / not_applicable.

target.title: Target

tool.title: Tool

applicable.title: Applicable
applicable.description: Whether a matching MFI import parser is registered for this format.

validated.title: Validated
validated.description: Whether validation actually ran in this runtime.

valid.title: Valid
valid.description: Whether the emitted artifact re-parsed cleanly when validation ran.

blocks_delivery.title: Blocks Delivery
blocks_delivery.description: Whether the export job must fail before packaging/delivery. ``True`` only when a validator ran and rejected the artifact.

warns.title: Warns
warns.description: Whether the report should surface a warning (toolchain unavailable). ``True`` only for a ``skipped`` verdict.

findings.title: Findings
findings.description: Structured parser/toolchain failures. Empty on a passing or skipped run.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Why validation did not run (not applicable, or toolchain unavailable).

headline.title: Headline
headline.description: Short banner heading for the validation gate.

message.title: Message
message.description: The full, ready-to-display validation sentence. Render verbatim.

EmittedValidationReport.title: EmittedValidationReport
EmittedValidationReport.description:
The validation gate + structured report for one emitted artifact (MFX-5.3).

Pairs the coarse :class:`ValidationVerdict` with structured findings and ready-to-render
:attr:`headline` / :attr:`message` copy. The single gate export surfaces read is
:attr:`blocks_delivery` (``True`` only for ``invalid``) and :attr:`warns` (``True`` only
for ``skipped``).

format.title: Format
format.description: Output format key this emitter produces, e.g. ``openapi-3.1``.

label.title: Label
label.description: Human label for target cards / CLI listings.

description.title: Description
description.description: One-line description of what it exports.
description.example: A pet available for adoption in the store.

icon.title: Icon
icon.description: Icon name (Lucide) the UI renders for this target's card.

paradigm.description: The canonical paradigm this emitter primarily targets.

multi_file.title: Multi File
multi_file.description: Whether the emitter produces a multi-file bundle (vs one artifact).

needs_toolchain.title: Needs Toolchain
needs_toolchain.description: Whether emit hard-requires an external toolchain binary.

available.title: Available
available.description: Whether this emitter can run in the current runtime.

unavailable_reason.title: Unavailable Reason
unavailable_reason.description: Human-readable reason the target is unavailable, or ``null`` when available.

EmitterDescriptor.title: EmitterDescriptor
EmitterDescriptor.description: Self-description of an export target for UI/CLI/REST enumeration (MFX-1.1).

entity.title: Entity
entity.description: Canonical type key of the entity (``acme.Pet``).

status.title: Status
status.description: ``pass`` — every checked instance validated; ``fail`` — the emitted schema rejected at least one source-valid instance; ``transcode_failed`` — no conformance failures, but at least one instance had no wire representation; ``missing`` — the emitted schema does not define this entity at all; ``skipped`` — no source-valid instance could be checked (see ``reason``).

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the entity was skipped or reported missing. ``None`` when checked.

instances_checked.title: Instances Checked
instances_checked.description: How many source-valid instances actually reached this target's validator (transcode failures are excluded — those instances were never judged).

failures.title: Failures

EntityTargetConformance.title: EntityTargetConformance
EntityTargetConformance.description: Instance-level conformance of one entity against one emitted target schema.

EnvironmentResponse.title: EnvironmentResponse
EnvironmentResponse.description: Lane state: what is serving, how far it reached, and against what budget.

EventReceiptResponse.title: EventReceiptResponse
EventReceiptResponse.description: The outcome of a webhook delivery.

ExceptionResponse.description: The outcome of opening a carve-out.

show.description: Whether to surface the advisory at all. ``False`` for a lossless export (or one whose losses are all below the requested severity threshold); consumers hide their banner when this is ``False``.

severity.description: The worst severity among the lossy constructs, driving how loudly the surface flags the export. ``None`` for a lossless export.

requires_ack.title: Requires Ack
requires_ack.description: Whether the export warrants an explicit dismiss-to-proceed acknowledgement — ``True`` only when a ``critical`` construct is lost.

target_format.title: Target Format
target_format.description: Human label for the target format woven into the copy (e.g. ``Protobuf``, ``OpenAPI 3.1``).

synthesized.title: Synthesized
synthesized.description: Number of constructs invented to satisfy the target (SYNTH).

affected.title: Affected
affected.description: Total constructs changed by the export (``dropped + approximated + synthesized``) — the count woven into the message.

headline.title: Headline
headline.description: Short banner heading for the advisory (or the lossless reassurance heading when :attr:`show` is ``False``).

message.title: Message
message.description: The full, ready-to-display advisory sentence. Consumers render this verbatim — they must not re-template it — so wording is identical across UI, browse, and CLI.

ExportAdvisory.title: ExportAdvisory
ExportAdvisory.description:
The single user-facing advisory for one cross-format (or lossy) export.

Built from a :class:`~app.lossiness.LossinessReport` and a human target label by
:func:`build_export_advisory`, then carried verbatim in the export / dry-run REST
response (MFX-2.5) so every surface — apiome-ui (MFX-6.2), apiome-browse
(MFX-7.2), apiome-cli (MFX-8.2) — renders identical wording.

The two acceptance criteria of MFX-2.4 are properties of this model:

* **reflects real counts** — ``dropped`` / ``approximated`` / ``synthesized`` and
  the ``{constructs}`` woven into ``message`` come straight from the report's
  per-kind counts, so the copy can never drift from the loss it describes;
* **shown when lossy, hidden when lossless** — :attr:`show` is ``False`` for a
  clean export (or one whose only losses fall below the caller's severity
  threshold), and consumers gate their banner on it.

id.title: Id
id.description: Row id, absent before it is written.

endpoint.title: Endpoint
endpoint.description: The collector endpoint. HTTPS by refusal.

headerSecretRef.title: Headersecretref
headerSecretRef.description: Name of the secret holding the authorization header. Never a value.

edgeAttached.title: Edgeattached
edgeAttached.description: False. Nothing collects, so nothing was ever shipped.

ExportBody.title: ExportBody
ExportBody.description: One OTLP export destination. A secret reference, never a header value.

path.title: Path
path.description: Relative path within the output bundle.

content.title: Content
content.description: The emitted file's content (structured document or text).

media_type.title: Media Type
media_type.description: Per-file media type when it differs from the bundle default.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: Schema Registry subject when the target assigns one (e.g. Avro).

ExportDispatchFile.title: ExportDispatchFile
ExportDispatchFile.description:
One emitted file returned inline by the dispatch surface (MFX-3.2).

Unlike the async job's metadata-only manifest (the bytes are served later by MFX-4.x),
a synchronous dispatch returns the ``content`` inline — there is no job to poll and no
separate download step.

version.title: Version

target.description: Target emitter key (``openapi``) or format key (``openapi-3.1``).

options.description: Per-target emit options (MFX-1.4); null or empty applies the target defaults.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: When true, stop after the fidelity report: no artifact is emitted.

confirm.title: Confirm
confirm.description: When true, proceed with a **severe** conversion (MFX-3.3) the transcoding guard would otherwise block with 409. Ignored for non-severe conversions and dry-runs.

min_severity.description: Lowest loss severity that raises the advisory (MFX-2.4); does not affect the report or counts.

ExportDispatchRequest.title: ExportDispatchRequest
ExportDispatchRequest.description: A dispatch request: source revision + chosen target + options + dry-run flag (MFX-3.2).

artifact.title: Artifact
artifact.description: The artifact (project) id the dispatch exported.

version.title: Version
version.description: The version selector as requested (label, UUID, or null).

target.title: Target
target.description: The resolved target format key (e.g. ``openapi-3.1``).

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: True when the dispatch stopped after the fidelity report.

fidelity.description: The full fidelity envelope (target + tier + report + advisory).

files.title: Files
files.description: The emitted files (inline); empty for a dry-run.

media_type.title: Media Type
media_type.description: The bundle's primary media type; null for a dry-run.

ExportDispatchResponse.title: ExportDispatchResponse
ExportDispatchResponse.description: The dispatch result: resolved coordinates + fidelity envelope + emitted artifact (MFX-3.2).

version.title: Version
version.description: Revision UUID, version label (``1.0.0``), or null for the latest revision.

target.title: Target
target.description: Target emitter key (``asyncapi``) or format key (``asyncapi-3``).

options.title: Options
options.description: Per-target emit options (MFX-1.4); null or empty applies the target defaults.

ExportDocumentRequest.title: ExportDocumentRequest
ExportDocumentRequest.description: An emit request: source revision + chosen target + per-emit options (MFX-11.5).

target.description: The resolved target emitter's descriptor (key/format/label/paradigm/…).

summary.description: The coarse tier / preserved-% summary, matching the /export/targets badge.

report.description: The full per-construct lossiness report (DROP/APPROX/SYNTH/OK + severity).

advisory.description: The user-facing 'may lose fidelity' advisory (MFX-2.4), shown when lossy.

projection.description: The bounded projection-manifest summary (EFP-1.1): the snapshot hash, target/version provenance, and status/reason counts that reconcile with ``report``. The full source→target node/edge graph is fetched page by page; this summary is what lets a preview, a verify, a CLI JSON dump, and a completed job reference one snapshot.

ExportFidelity.title: ExportFidelity
ExportFidelity.description:
The full fidelity envelope for one (source, target) export (MFX-2.5).

The heavyweight half of the surface, returned by ``POST /export/preview`` and *embedded
verbatim in an export job's result* (MFX-3.1/3.2): the target descriptor, the coarse
:class:`TargetFidelity` summary, the whole :class:`~app.lossiness.LossinessReport`
(per-construct detail), and the user-facing :class:`~app.fidelity_advisory.ExportAdvisory`.
Because every field is derived purely from the prediction engine, a preview and the export
it previews carry identical fidelity.

ExportFidelityTier.title: ExportFidelityTier
ExportFidelityTier.description:
The one-word fidelity badge shown on a target's export card (MFX-6.1).

A coarse, at-a-glance summary of a full :class:`~app.lossiness.LossinessReport` — the
detail lives in the report, this is the headline. Derived from the source's construct
classes vs the target's capability profile (see :func:`classify_tier`).

status_path.title: Status Path
status_path.description: Relative URL path for GET …/jobs/{job_id} until the job reaches a terminal state.

ExportJobAccepted.title: ExportJobAccepted
ExportJobAccepted.description: Returned when a job is accepted (HTTP 202) — mirrors the import acceptance.

code.title: Code
code.description: Stable delivery-taxonomy error code (additive-only; same as the terminal error event).

category.title: Category
category.description: Taxonomy category: input, format, capability, policy, resource, transport, or internal.

retriable.title: Retriable
retriable.description: Whether retrying the identical request may succeed without changing the input.

context.title: Context
context.description: Structured detail (e.g. an upstream ``status_code`` or guard reasons).

correlation_id.title: Correlation Id
correlation_id.description: Correlation id of the request that started the job (IXH-6.6) — equal to the X-Request-ID echoed on the submitting 202 response. Quote it in bug reports; it links the failure to every log line the job emitted.

ExportJobError.title: ExportJobError
ExportJobError.description:
Structured terminal error for a ``failed`` export job (MFX-3.4 / IXH-6.4).

The machine-readable twin of a job's terminal error event: a poller shows ``message``
and branches on ``code`` (e.g. distinguish ``TRANSCODE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`` — resubmit
with ``confirm`` — from ``SOURCE_LOAD_FAILED``) without scraping the free-form event log.

``code`` / ``category`` / ``remediation`` / ``retriable`` come from the delivery error
taxonomy (:mod:`app.delivery_error_taxonomy`) and are additive-only, so UI remediation
copy and CLI exit codes can key off them safely.

ExportJobEvent.title: ExportJobEvent
ExportJobEvent.description: Structured log line from an export job (same shape as an import job event).

path.title: Path
path.description: Relative path within the output bundle.

media_type.title: Media Type
media_type.description: The file's media type when it differs from the bundle default.

size_bytes.title: Size Bytes
size_bytes.description: Serialized size of the file's content in bytes.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: Schema Registry subject when the target assigns one (e.g. Avro).

ExportJobFile.title: ExportJobFile
ExportJobFile.description:
One emitted file's manifest entry — metadata only, never the content.

The delivery epics (MFX-4.x) serve the bytes; the job result carries just enough
for a caller to show what was produced and how large it is.

target.title: Target

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: True when the job is a fidelity-only dry-run.

ExportJobListItem.description: Summary row for GET …/jobs (no event log, no full fidelity envelope).

total.title: Total
total.description: Total pipeline stages for this job.

current_item.title: Current Item
current_item.description: Human hint for the stage (e.g. the target key).

ExportJobProgress.title: ExportJobProgress
ExportJobProgress.description: Coarse-grained progress snapshot (mirrors the import job's progress shape).

artifact.title: Artifact
artifact.description: The artifact (project) id the job exported.

target.title: Target
target.description: The resolved target format key (e.g. ``openapi-3.1``).

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: True when the job stopped after the fidelity report.

snapshot_hash.title: Snapshot Hash
snapshot_hash.description: The projection snapshot hash this job computed (EFP-2.1) — the same ``fidelity.projection.manifest_hash`` a preview/verify of identical inputs returns. Recorded so the completed job is attributable to one exact snapshot.

options.title: Options
options.description: The per-target emit options the job was submitted with (EFP-2.1) — the configuration half of the snapshot record; null when the target defaults applied.

fidelity.description: The full fidelity envelope (target + tier + report + advisory).

guard.description: The pre-flight transcoding guard (MFX-3.3): the conversion band and why. A severe conversion only completes when it was submitted with ``confirm``.

validation.description: The emitted-artifact validation gate + report (MFX-5.3). Set on a completed real export after the MFX-5.1 re-parse; null for a dry-run (no artifact).

delivery.description: The delivery gate decision (IXH-2.5): the single ``allow`` / ``allow_with_warning`` / ``block`` verdict over the emitted validation, the source's lint grade, the projected fidelity floor, and the tenant's export policy — with its named reasons and the signed attestation attached to the delivered artifact. Null for a dry-run (nothing is delivered).

media_type.title: Media Type
media_type.description: The bundle's primary media type; null for a dry-run.

download_path.description: Relative URL a poller dereferences to fetch the emitted artifact bundle (served by the delivery epics, MFX-4.x). Set once a real export completes; null for a dry-run (no artifact was emitted).

ExportJobResult.title: ExportJobResult

What a terminal ``completed`` export job produced.

Carries the resolved source coordinates, the resolved target, the full
:class:`~app.export_fidelity.ExportFidelity` envelope (identical to a ``/export/preview``
of the same inputs), and — for a real (non-dry-run) export — the emitted file manifest.

Request body for export job start.

target.title: Target
target.description: Target emitter key (``openapi``) or format key (``openapi-3.1``).

anyOf.description: Request body for export job start.
Request body for export job start.

options.title: Options
options.description: Per-target emit options (MFX-1.4); null or empty applies the target defaults.

dry_run.title: Dry Run

confirm.title: Confirm
confirm.description: When true, proceed with a **severe** conversion (MFX-3.3) the transcoding guard would otherwise fail the job on. Ignored for non-severe conversions and dry-runs.

anyOf.description: Request body for export job start.
Request body for export job start.

acknowledged_snapshot.description: The projection snapshot hash (``fidelity.projection.manifest_hash``) the caller previewed and acknowledged (EFP-2.1). When set, the job recomputes the snapshot for its actual inputs and **fails with `STALE_PREVIEW`** if the hashes differ — the source revision, options, emitter version, or registry changed since the preview, so the acknowledgement no longer describes what would be generated. Null skips the check.

ExportJobStartRequest.title: ExportJobStartRequest
ExportJobStartRequest.description:
Submit an export job: source coordinates + target + options + dry-run flag.

(MFX-2.5/11.5); ``dry_run`` selects the preview-only path (fidelity report, no

ExportRoundtripResponse.title: ExportRoundtripResponse
ExportRoundtripResponse.description:
The round-trip comparison result the Export Studio renders (IXH-4.4).

``status`` speaks the IXH-1.7 matrix's vocabulary so a Studio run over a corpus
entry reconciles with the published matrix cell:

* ``pass`` — every empirical difference is explained by the fidelity report and
  nothing over-claims preservation;
* ``fail`` — at least one unexplained difference or over-claim (a fidelity bug
  worth reporting), or the emitted artifact could not be re-imported at all;
* ``unsupported`` — the comparison was **skipped with an explanation** (no import
  adapter can re-ingest the emit format, or the emitter is unavailable here).

The three difference groups are exactly the reconciliation's: ``matched``
(explained by the report — expected loss), ``unexplained`` (the report does not
account for them), and ``overclaims`` (the report claimed preservation reality
contradicts). The provenance fields (`emitter_version` / `apiome_version` /
`registry_version` / fingerprints) give an unexplained difference's issue report
its reproduction coordinates without shipping any source bytes.

ExportVerifyVerdict.title: ExportVerifyVerdict

The overall go/no-go verdict for a one-call verify (MFX-42.1/42.5).

The single band the Verify workbench's banner and Generate gate read, derived from the
validation gate (MFX-5.3) and the fidelity tier (MFX-2.5) per the MFX-3.3 severity classes:

* ``clean`` — a lossless conversion whose emitted artifact validated (or had nothing to
  validate); the green path.
* ``lossy`` — a valid artifact, but the conversion is not lossless; the user may proceed only
  after acknowledging the loss.
* ``invalid`` — a validator ran and rejected the emitted artifact; the export is blocked and no
  acknowledgement can override it.
